content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To get a tattoo of a rose, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Choose the specific shade of red for the petals (20 minutes)
Step 2. Research local tattoo shops with high ratings (2 hours)
Step 3. Apply a thin layer of specialized tattoo ointment (5 minutes)
Step 4. Browse the artist's digital portfolio (30 minutes)
Step 5. Watch the artist set up the sterile needle cartridge (5 minutes)
Step 6. Read through the shop's liability waiver (15 minutes)
Step 7. Clean the skin area with isopropyl alcohol (2 minutes)
Step 8. Pour the black lining ink into small disposable cups (2 minutes)
Step 9. Final inspection of the completed rose in the mirror (3 minutes)
Step 10. Pay the remaining balance for the session (10 minutes)
Step 11. Discuss the hourly rate with the shop manager (15 minutes)
Step 12. Book a consultation appointment on the calendar (10 minutes)
Step 13. Shave the area of skin where the rose will go (5 minutes)
Step 14. Check the artist's availability for the upcoming weekend (10 minutes)
Step 15. Save reference photos of realistic roses to a phone (30 minutes)
Step 16. Prepare the tattoo machine by connecting the power supply (10 minutes)
Step 17. The artist puts on a fresh pair of nitrile gloves (1 minute)
Step 18. Outline the outer edges of the rose leaves (45 minutes)
Step 19. Set the chair to a comfortable height for the artist (2 minutes)
Step 20. Apply the stencil transfer gel to the skin (2 minutes)
Step 21. Draw a custom rose sketch based on references (3 hours)
Step 22. Take a "before" photo of the blank skin (1 minute)
Step 23. Place a protective barrier film over the workstation (10 minutes)
Step 24. Visit the shop in person to check for cleanliness (1 hour)
Step 25. Wrap the finished tattoo in medical-grade bandages (10 minutes)
Step 26. Organize the different sizes of shading needles (5 minutes)
Step 27. Place the rose stencil onto the prepared skin (5 minutes)
Step 28. Confirm the total price estimate for the piece (10 minutes)
Step 29. Finalize the size and dimensions of the rose (20 minutes)
Step 30. Mix a custom pink wash for the petal highlights (10 minutes)
Step 31. Set aside a cash tip for the artist (5 minutes)
Step 32. Print the final rose design onto stencil paper (5 minutes)
Step 33. Lay out the green ink pigments for the stem (5 minutes)
Step 34. Verify the spelling of any text accompanying the rose (5 minutes)
Step 35. Ink the dark shadows deep within the rose petals (1 hour)
Step 36. Eat a high-protein meal before the session (45 minutes)
Step 37. Drink a large bottle of water for hydration (10 minutes)
Step 38. Sign the physical consent form at the front desk (5 minutes)
Step 39. Blend the red ink into the pink highlights (40 minutes)
Step 40. Select the specific brand of organic inks to be used (15 minutes)
Step 41. Compare different rose petal styles (color vs. black and grey) (1 hour)
Step 42. Add white ink highlights for a dew-drop effect (15 minutes)
Step 43. Measure the width of the forearm for placement (5 minutes)
Step 44. Complete the intricate shading of the rose petals (2 hours)
Step 45. Review the aftercare instructions provided by the shop (10 minutes)
Step 46. Begin the line work for the rose stem and thorns (1 hour)
Step 47. Clean the tattooed area with green soap (5 minutes)
Step 48. Fill in the vibrant red color of the rose (90 minutes)
Step 49. Check the weather to ensure a comfortable commute (5 minutes)
Step 50. Withdraw cash from the ATM for the deposit (15 minutes)
Step 51. Look up the artist's Instagram for recent work (20 minutes)
Step 52. Take an "after" photo of the vibrant rose (2 minutes)
Step 53. Adjust the lighting in the studio for better visibility (5 minutes)
Step 54. Wipe away excess ink during the process (30 minutes)
Step 55. Pay the initial deposit to secure the time slot (5 minutes)
Step 56. Sit in the tattoo chair and get comfortable (5 minutes)
Step 57. Wash hands thoroughly before entering the booth (3 minutes)
Step 58. Apply a soothing finishing spray to the skin (2 minutes)
Step 59. Double-check the stencil alignment in the mirror (5 minutes)
Step 60. Remove any jewelry near the tattoo site (2 minutes)
